events.message: change categorical_encoding from 'onehot' to 'ordinal' to rank categories by their out-of-fold relationship to the target, reducing spurious feature dimensions and improving precision; also add numeric_transform 'log' to handle any right-skewed non-negative columns that may be inflating noise in the feature space

switch model from lightgbm to xgboost to gain more expressive capacity for the reduced feature set; xgboost's regularization and interaction handling will better utilize the 19 ordinal/log-transformed features without requiring the sparse 45-feature space. Keep use_class_weighting=false for now since class balance is not severely imbalanced.

revert numeric_transform from 'log' to 'none' and change categorical_encoding from 'ordinal' to 'target' to restore discriminative power while keeping dimensionality manageable. Target encoding will rank categories by their direct relationship to the outcome (unlike ordinal's out-of-fold ranking), and removing the log transform will preserve the original scale information for numeric features. This should recover precision without returning to the 45-feature sparse space.

Enable use_class_weighting=true on xgboost (which will apply scale_pos_weight internally) to shift the model's learned decision boundary toward the minority class during training, reducing reliance on threshold manipulation. This is a training-time correction that works with the model's regularization rather than against it, unlike the current low threshold (0.229) which is a post-hoc band-aid. Keep categorical_encoding at 'target' and numeric_transform at 'none' since AUC-ROC is stable; the problem is precision collapse from threshold drift, not feature weakness.

diagnosis.failure_mode: Precision_pos has deteriorated from 0.5565 (iteration 2) to 0.4867 (iteration 4) while recall_pos climbed to 0.8342. The model is now aggressively flagging positives with a very low threshold (0.229), generating excessive false positives. AUC-ROC is stable at ~0.847, indicating the model has adequate discriminative capacity, but the decision boundary is misaligned. XGBoost with max_depth=2 and target encoding is too permissive; the shallow tree combined with target-encoded features that directly encode class relationship is pushing the model toward the minority class without sufficient regularization to maintain precision.

diagnosis.failure_mode: Random forest with use_class_weighting=true and max_depth=19 is severely overfitting: train_auc_roc=0.9998 vs test_auc_roc=0.84 (train_test_gap=0.1598). The model memorized the training data rather than learning generalizable patterns. Test AUC-ROC dropped from 0.8471 (iteration 4) to 0.84, and precision_pos remains stuck at 0.5472. The deep tree (max_depth=19) with class weighting is too expressive for the 19-feature space and is overfitting despite the weighting.
diagnosis.instruction: switch model from random_forest to logistic_regression with use_class_weighting=true. Logistic regression is a linear model that cannot overfit in the same way—it will force the model to learn a simple, generalizable decision boundary while class weighting shifts that boundary toward the minority class during training. This eliminates the memorization problem while preserving the class-weighting correction. Keep categorical_encoding at 'target' and numeric_transform at 'none'.
